comment: Which library PDF is scored against which reference, and why. Read library_pairs.py for the
rules. Evidence quoted below is from reports/library/drift.json: 'pitch agreement' is the
fraction of reference notes whose pitch appears anywhere in the transcription, which no timing
error can move - it falls only when the two are different music, or when the source is read so
badly that the notes are not recovered at all.
Statuses: confirmed (same arrangement, evidence agrees), candidate (plausible, unverified,
summarised separately so it cannot join a headline), rejected (a pairing that looks right and
must not be made, with the reason).

pairs.pdf: Arr. Alice Lefebvre - Bella Ciao - Piano
pairs.reference: midi/custom/Arr. Alice Lefebvre - Bella Ciao - Piano.mid
pairs.why: Same arranger named in both filenames. Pitch agreement 0.948, note ratio 0.948, span 0.99.

pairs.pdf: Composed by Yu-peng Chen_Arr by Prower's Sheets - Liyue Battle Theme 1
pairs.reference: midi/custom/Composed by Yu-peng Chen_Arr by Prower's Sheets - Liyue Battle Theme 1.mid
pairs.why: Pitch agreement 0.992 and note ratio 0.997 - as close to the same music as this sample gets.
Pitch agreement 1.000: every reference note is present. Note ratio 1.466 and span 1.41 are the engine over-producing, not a reference mismatch.

pairs.pdf: HOYO-MiX, Mika Kobayashi - Beyond This Station
pairs.reference: midi/custom/HOYO-MiX, Mika Kobayashi - Beyond This Station.mid

pairs.why: Filename match once punctuation is normalised, and the numbers agree: pitch agreement 0.948, note ratio 0.998. Missed entirely by the old filename-equality rule.

pairs.pdf: - If I can Stop One Heart From Breaking
pairs.reference: midi/custom/If I can Stop One Heart From Breaking.mid
pairs.why: Pitch agreement 0.959, note ratio 0.975. Missed by filename equality because of the leading dash, and it is the more useful of the two PDFs of this piece: it validates the reference that the other PDF appeared to impugn.

pairs.pdf: If I Can Stop One Heart From Breaking
pairs.reference: midi/custom/If I can Stop One Heart From Breaking.mid
pairs.why: Pitch agreement 0.734 against the same reference the PDF above scores 0.959 on. That rules out the reference and indicts this source: same music, same truth, six pages each, and the engine recovers a quarter less of it here. Keep it - a controlled pair of sources with the reference held fixed is the only place source quality can be measured apart from score length.

Pitch agreement 0.735 and span 0.783 - the reference is a quarter longer than the transcription, which is what a repeat the printed page does not expand looks like. Same piece, probably not the same edition.
Pitch agreement 0.817 with note ratio 0.819 and span 0.687: the same music is plausibly there, but a third of the timeline is not. Unresolved.

Pitch agreement 0.657 at span 0.996 - right length, a third of the notes unaccounted for. Either a different edition or a badly read source; the one-page PDF of the same title below does not help decide.

pairs.reference: midi/custom/Original Art by HOYO-MIX - Coronal Radiance.mid
pairs.why: Pitch agreement 0.785 but span 0.593: the transcription is little more than half the reference's length. Needs a MusicXML reference before it means anything.

One page, 288 notes against the reference's 1764, span 0.246, pitch agreement 0.163. This PDF is an excerpt of the piece, not the piece, so scoring it against a full reference measures nothing about the engine.
Two pages, pitch agreement 0.337, note ratio 0.342, span 0.342. Like the IN THE POOL excerpt above, this is a fraction of the music the reference contains.

pairs.pdf: Dark Souls - Gwyn Lord of Cinder
pairs.why: Different arrangement. The PDF carries Finale 2014 metadata naming it 'Gwyn, Lord of Cinder (Two Pianos)'; the reference is a solo MuseScore MIDI with 2852 notes against the transcription's 1534. Pitch agreement 0.538 - a third of the reference is music that is not on this page. Its onset F1 of 0.186 was never an engine result, and it was the 13-page point anchoring the top of the page-count correlation.

pairs.pdf: Yu-peng Chen_Arr_ musescore.com_munzutai - Rapid as Wildfires　／　Liyue Battle Theme I
pairs.why: Same piece as the confirmed Liyue entry, different arranger - munzutai here against Prower's Sheets in the reference. Filename similarity is high enough that a fuzzy matcher would pair them, and doing so would score one arrangement against another.
The only Unravel reference is Animenz's arrangement, which is a different and far denser piece. Do not pair on title alone.
The nearest reference is 'genshin1.mid', which names neither a piece nor an arranger. Pairing on a guess is how an invalid reference enters the sample; it needs the user to say what genshin1 is.
